textPlacement.assessment: Pass on the complete r05 topic row, detail, references and 18–24-month placement. “Fitting shapes and opening lids” now identifies the situation before the reader reaches the summary. The whole entry remains a source-attributed perspective on repeated movements: taking pieces off is valid, matching can come later, difficulty can be reduced, and materials are examples rather than a required collection. Age variants and small-part supervision stay public. No new procedure, child deadline or parent performance expectation is introduced by the concrete title.

Pass on the complete r05 topic row and detail. The readiness line now follows stopping, pointing, listening or looking together, so it supports the actual invitation instead of adding a material-handling requirement. Leaves, clouds and insects make the short row useful on its own. The full entry preserves adult time, quiet shared attention, finding a name later, and alternatives for a family without outdoor space. It does not require a lesson, equipment or a daily quota.

Pass on the complete r05 topic row and detail. The new readiness wording concerns current movements and available space, consistent with dancing, running and playing with a ball. The short row remains a descriptive perspective, and the body keeps indoor space constraints, the outdoor ball example and differing equipment contexts without presenting a progression to achieve at eighteen to twenty-four months. The broader title is understandable with these concrete examples; the replacement does not warrant a new blanket title change.

Pass on the complete r05 Play & discovery and A home that helps rows and the full detail. The short text offers familiar favorites and open-ended home play without implying pretend play is expected at this age. The cue now concerns exploring a toy. Both the public age context and the rewritten paragraph distinguish the unaged home discussion from Davies's separate around-two-and-a-half-and-later pretend-play passage; the explicit note prevents an eighteen-to-twenty-four-month expectation. The corrected original section title and PDF 103–104 reference lead to the actual discussion and its continuation. Material fit, supervision, rest and avoiding a duplicated classroom remain visible. Attribution does not become a new developmental deadline or a ban on imaginative play.

issueResolutions.assessment: The exact replacement title is “Fitting shapes and opening lids” in both the rendered topic row and detail heading. It names the supported actions while preserving the interest-led perspective and existing qualifications.

The exact readiness replacement is “Follow what catches your child’s attention as they stop, point, listen, or look with you.” The materials clause is gone, and the whole entry still allows limited adult time and families without home outdoor space.

The exact readiness replacement is “Follow your child’s current movements and the space available.” The equipment paragraph retains its different ages/readiness and no-achievement-list qualification; no apparatus instructions were added.

The reference now includes PDF 103–104 and names imagination, pretend play around two and a half and later, and artistic creativity. The full replacement also distinguishes the two source discussions in the body and public age context and removes the cue that could imply pretend play is expected at eighteen to twenty-four months. The source pages were personally reread before resolving this issue.
